c.title: Proposal 2026-1
c.pre: A proposal to convene a constitutional convention for the purpose of drafting a general revision of the state constitution
c.q: Shall a convention of elected delegates be convened in 2027 to draft a general revision of the State Constitution for presentation to the state’s voters for their approval or rejection?

c.title: Proposal 2026-2
c.pre: A proposed initiated law to prohibit campaign contributions from certain regulated utilities and government contractors and apply campaign finance laws and regulations to additional types of political communications
c.q:
The proposal would:

• Prohibit regulated electric and gas utilities, contractors with over $250,000 annually in government contracts, and people and organizations with substantial connections to these utilities/contractors from making direct or indirect campaign contributions to those who run for or hold offices that impact them.

• Expand laws regulating spending on political communications, including those requiring disclosing donor information, to apply to communications clearly identifying candidates or ballot questions, even if they do not expressly advocate voting for/against them.

• Expressly apply the law requiring disclosure of who paid for political communications to internet political communications.

Should this proposal be adopted?

c.title: Huron County Public Safety Millage Proposal
c.q:
For the purpose of providing for public safety within Huron County, including law enforcement services and equipment, jail operations, courthouse security, emergency medical services, and other public safety functions within the County, shall the constitutional limitation on general ad valorem taxes which may be assessed in any one year upon all property within Huron County, Michigan, be increased by up to 0.4000 mills ($0.4000 per $1,000.00 of taxable value) for a period of ten (10) years, from 2026 through 2035, inclusive?

If approved and levied in full, this millage will raise an estimated $1,220,546 for public safety purposes within the County in the first calendar year of the levy. In accordance with State law, a portion of the millage may also be captured by the DDA/TIFA of the City of Bad Axe and Village of Port Austin, and the DDA of the City of Caseville and the Villages of Elkton and Sebewaing.

c.title: Proposed Initiated Ordinance Regarding Marihuana Establishments
c.q: Shall the City of Bad Axe repeal Ordinance No. 2019-3 which prohibits marihuana establishments and instead allow up to two such establishments to operate in the City in accordance with the Michigan Regulation and Taxation of Marihuana Act.

c.title: Lake Township Road Maintenance and Spongy Moth Suppression Millage Renewal Proposal
c.q: Shall the previously voted increase in the tax rate limitation imposed under Article IX, Section 6 of the Michigan Constitution on general ad valorem taxes in Lake Township, Huron County, of 1.50 mills ($1.50 per $1,000 of taxable value), as reduced to 1.4395 mills ($1.4395 per $1,000 of taxable value) by the required millage rollbacks, be renewed at the rolled-back rate of 1.4395 mills ($1.4395 per $1,000 of taxable value), and shall the Township levy such millage annually for four (4) years, 2027 through 2030, inclusive, to provide funds for general operating expenses to be designated for road maintenance and spongy moth suppression, thereby raising an estimated $212,057 in the first year of the levy?

c.title: Lake Township Road Millage Renewal Proposal
c.q: Shall the previously voted increase in the tax rate limitation imposed under Article IX, Section 6 of the Michigan Constitution on general ad valorem taxes in Lake Township, Huron County, of 1.0 mills ($1.00 per $1,000 of taxable value), as reduced to 0.9561 mills ($0.9561 per $1,000 of taxable value) by the required millage rollbacks, be renewed at the rolled-back rate of 0.9561 mills ($0.9561 per $1,000 of taxable value), and shall the Township levy such millage annually for four (4) years, 2027 through 2030, inclusive, to provide funds for road construction and maintenance, thereby raising an estimated $140,846 in the first year of the levy?

c.title: City of Caseville Millage Proposal for Mosquito and Pest Control
c.q: Shall the tax limitation on general ad valorem taxes within the City of Caseville imposed under Article IX, Sec. 6 of the Michigan Constitution be increased by .6 mills ($0.60 per $1,000 of taxable value) for a period of five (5) years, 2027 through 2031 inclusive, for the purpose of funding the monitoring and suppression of mosquitos, spongy moths, and other pest species within the City, and shall the City levy such increase in millage, which, if levied in full would raise an estimated $36,442.00 in the first year.

c.title: City of Caseville Millage Proposal for Police Protection
c.q: Shall the tax limitation on general ad valorem taxes within the City of Caseville imposed under Article IX, Sec. 6 of the Michigan Constitution be increased by .6 mills ($0.60 per $1,000 of taxable value) for a period of five (5) years, 2027 through 2031 inclusive, for the purpose of funding police protection including law enforcement personnel, equipment, training, and department operating expenses, and shall the City levy such increase in millage, which, if levied in full would raise an estimated $36,442.00 in the first year.

c.title: Winsor Township Fire Protection and Emergency Services Millage Proposal
c.q:
Shall Winsor Township increase the tax rate limitation imposed under Article IX, Section 6 of the Michigan Constitution and levy a new additional millage of 1.0 mills ($1.00 per $1,000 of taxable value) on taxable property within Winsor Township annually for four (4) years, 2026 through 2029, inclusive, for the purposes of funding fire protection and emergency services in the Township, including contracting for emergency medical response services and paying operating and capital expenses of the Winsor Township Fire Department?

If approved and levied, this millage would raise an estimated $197,505 in the first year of the levy.

c.title: Village of Pigeon Headlee Override Ballot Proposal
c.q:
Shall a “Headlee Override” be adopted so that the current limitations on the amount of Village taxes that may be levied against all taxable property in the Village of Pigeon, Huron County, Michigan be increased as follows:

Up to 12.500 mills ($12.50 per $1,000 of taxable value) from approximately 12.500 mills ($12.50 per $1000 of taxable value) for ten years, 2027 to 2037 inclusive for general operating expenses,

Up to 5.000 mills ($5.00 per $1,000 of taxable value) from approximately 5.000 mills ($5.00 per $1000 of taxable value) for ten (10) years, 2027 to 2037 inclusive for Street Repairs and Improvement, and

Up to 1.500 mills ($1.50 per $1,000 of taxable value) from approximately 1.500 mills ($1.50 per $1,000 of taxable value) for ten (10) years, 2027 to 2037 inclusive for Water Fund Debt?

If approved and levied in its entirely, this millage would raise and estimated maximum amount of $0.00 for the Village in 2027 by allowing the Village to levy the maximum mills previously approved by voters and authorized by the Village Charter and the State Law which have been reduced as required by the Michigan Constitution of 1963.

c.title: Proposal for Road Millage Renewal
c.q: Shall the previous voted increase in the tax limitation imposed under Article IX, Sec. 6 of the Michigan Constitution on general ad valorem taxes within Port Austin Township be renewed at 1.50 mills ($1.50 per $1,000 of taxable value) for the period of 2026 through 2035 inclusive for township road repairs, road maintenance, tree trimming and street light installation, operation and repair, and shall the Township levy such renewal in millage for said purpose, thereby raising in the first year an estimated $200,000.00.

c.title: Renewal of Millage for Road Improvements Proposition
c.q: Shall the tax limitation imposed under Article IX, Sec. 6 of the Michigan Constitution on general ad valorem taxes within Dwight Township be renewed for said Township by 2.00 mills ($2.00 per $1,000 of taxable value) for the period of 2027 through 2031 inclusive for road improvements within the Township; and shall the Township levy such renewal for said purpose, thereby raising in the first year an estimated $164,000.00?
